audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Akshan level 1, but both spikes[0] and whys[0] on the same page say 'Warwick owns level 1' and explain exactly why. The chart and the prose contradict each other on the very first stage.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast heals off max-health damage from level 1 and Eternal Hunger heals on every basic attack below 50% health, tripling below 25%. Akshan at level 1 has one Avengerang and a single extra passive shot. The prose is right and the chart is wrong, so I flipped win[0] to Warwick rather than rewrite two correct strings. The packet also carries a stale defect claiming the chart gives Akshan 5/7 stages — the chart on disk gives Akshan 2, so that defect is already resolved.
audit.corrected: NOT APPLIED — flagged for the user instead. A one-word side flip cannot pass the +/-10% length gate ('Akshan' 6 chars -> 'Warwick' 7 chars, +16.7%), so the applier would reject it. Either the chart's win[0] must become Warwick or spikes[0] and whys[0] must stop saying Warwick owns level 1; I did not guess which.

audit.why: Warwick's level 1, Akshan's 2-3 tools, the Youmuu's-plus-Executioner's spike, and Warwick's late sustain. Four spikes, correctly placed; the entry is unusually good at putting the anti-heal buy on the spike where it belongs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned anywhere in the entry — not in early, mid, late, any why, any spike, or either wants list. It is the ability that most directly answers Akshan.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second.' Against a burst champion that is a 15s button which both blanks the damage window and then removes Akshan's control of his own spacing. Also missing: Infinite Duress 'leaps in a direction (SCALING WITH HIS BONUS MOVE SPEED)', so Blood Hunt does not merely help him walk you down — it physically lengthens his ultimate's leap, which is why hunted Akshans get caught from ranges that look safe.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl (E, 15s): 2.5s damage reduction then a 1s fear. Infinite Duress leaps further the more bonus move speed he has, so Blood Hunt extends it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt is referenced five times without its cooldown, and Eternal Hunger is described only as ramping 'the lower his HP gets'.
audit.why: Blood Hunt is 80s at rank 1 — an enormous window, and knowing it changes whether you respect the hunt threshold at all. Eternal Hunger has two concrete gates rather than a ramp: healing below 50% health, tripled below 25%. The second gate is exactly the health range Comeuppance wants him in.
audit.corrected: Blood Hunt 80s at rank 1; Eternal Hunger heals under 50% and triples under 25%.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is already named in spikes[2], wants.you[2] and whys[5], correctly tied to blanking Jaws of the Beast and Eternal Hunger. Nothing to add.

edits.after: Leap Infinite Duress from further than looks safe — its range grows with Blood Hunt speed — and suppress you for 1.5s

edits.before: After 2+ items his missing-HP lifesteal ramps hardest exactly when you'd execute him, his W (Blood Hunt) speed closes any gap, and R suppress catches you mid-Heroic-Swing — he out-sustains and runs the lane down.
edits.after: After 2+ items Eternal Hunger triples below 25% exactly when you'd execute him, Blood Hunt speed closes any gap AND lengthens his R leap, and a 1.5s suppress catches you mid-swing — he out-sustains and runs you down.

edits.before: Warwick owns level 1 — his Q heals off damage dealt and his passive lifesteal ramps the lower his own HP gets, so your lone passive double-shot just feeds his sustain. Don't trade before you have a tool.
edits.after: Warwick owns level 1 — Jaws of the Beast heals off max-health damage and Eternal Hunger heals below 50% health then TRIPLES below 25%, so chipping him only feeds his sustain. Don't trade before you have a tool.

edits.before: Warwick wins the first level: his Q heals off the damage he deals and his passive lifesteal ramps up the lower HIS health gets, so your one passive double-shot does nothing but feed his sustain. Don't fight before you have a tool. The lane flips at 2-3 — your second passive shot and Avengerang out-and-back poke let you chip him faster than he heals, and E (Heroic Swing) at 3 means you can hook off terrain to reposition the instant he commits W (Blood Hunt) move speed at you. Pelt him with Q from max range, cancel your second shot for the move-speed kite, and never stand still long enough for him to close — a Warwick who can't stick to you can't drain.
edits.after: Warwick wins the first level: Jaws of the Beast (Q) heals off max-health damage and Eternal Hunger heals him below 50% and triples below 25%, so your one passive double-shot only feeds him. Don't fight before you have a tool. The lane opens at 2-3 — your second shot and the out-and-back Avengerang chip faster than he heals, and E (Heroic Swing) at 3 hooks off terrain the instant he commits Blood Hunt, which is only up every 80s at rank 1. Respect Primal Howl (E): 2.5 seconds of damage reduction, then a fear that takes your spacing away. Never stand still — a Warwick who can't stick can't drain.

edits.before: This is your strongest pure-laning stretch. Levels 4-5 are your peak window because you out-range his melee drain entirely and your E cooldown drops to 0.5s on any takedown, so a single pick snowballs instantly. Hold the spacing: Avengerang whenever it's up, double-shot when he steps to last-hit, and save E to swing AWAY the moment he commits W. At 6 he gets R (Infinite Duress), a point-blank suppress that locks you still and lets him drain — so respect his all-in range, bait the R or his W engage, then E out and re-poke. Your R (Comeuppance) stores bullets and fires for up to 200% bonus damage on his missing health, so it executes him from range better than his suppress can ever brawl you down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are contested, not conceded. You out-range his melee drain, but Primal Howl (E) is a 15s button giving 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then a fear that takes your spacing — it blanks a burst window and breaks your kite at once. Hold the spacing anyway: Avengerang whenever it's up, double-shot when he steps to last-hit, and save E to swing AWAY the moment he commits Blood Hunt. At 6, Infinite Duress suppresses 1.5s and its LEAP SCALES with his bonus move speed, so a hunted Akshan is a far longer jump than it looks. Bait it, E out, re-poke — Comeuppance executes off missing health from range better than his suppress can brawl.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your peak laning window: you out-range his melee drain and your E resets to a 0.5s cooldown on any takedown, so a pick snowballs instantly.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are contested: you out-range his drain, but Primal Howl cuts the damage he takes for 2.5s and then fears you clean off your spacing.

notes: Primal Howl appears nowhere in this entry — not once across early, mid, late, all seven whys, four spikes and both wants lists — despite being the ability that most directly answers a burst champion: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction followed by a fear. Added it to early, mid and whys[3]. The second real omission is that Infinite Duress leaps further the more bonus move speed Warwick has, which means Blood Hunt is not just a chase buff, it extends the ultimate's reach — that is why hunted Akshans get suppressed from distances that looked safe. I did NOT apply the level-1 chart fix: win[0] says Akshan while spikes[0] and whys[0] both say Warwick owns level 1, and a one-word side flip ('Akshan' to 'Warwick') is +16.7% length, which the applier's band rejects. That contradiction is left in place and raised as a question — the kit says Warwick is right. The packet's chart defect for this matchup is stale — the chart on disk already gives Akshan only 2 stages, not 5.
